title: Fronting and verb-second inversion
goal: Keep the finite verb in second position after fronting, including negative or restrictive openings, without carrying main-clause inversion into subordinate clauses.

objectives.statement: Keep the finite verb in second position after fronting, including negative or restrictive openings, without carrying main-clause inversion into subordinate clauses.

sections.title: A morning at the repair café

spans.value: Nora and Elias are preparing a neighborhood repair café. Nora can arrive early, but Elias depends on a bus that is often late.
I morgen åpner vi reparasjonskafeen klokka ni.

blocks.translation: Tomorrow we open the repair café at nine.

spans.value: Før klokka ni kan jeg ikke komme.
Det går bra. Først setter jeg fram bordene og verktøyet.

blocks.translation: That’s fine. First I’ll put out the tables and tools.

spans.value: Bare hvis bussen er i rute, er jeg der klokka ni.

blocks.translation: Only if the bus is on time will I be there at nine.

spans.value: Jeg vet at bussen ikke alltid er i rute.

blocks.translation: I know that the bus isn’t always on time.

spans.value: Aldri har den vært så forsinket som i går.

blocks.translation: It has never been as late as it was yesterday.

spans.value: Når du kommer, kan du lage kaffe.

blocks.translation: When you arrive, you can make coffee.

spans.value: Gjerne. Bare da fungerer jeg ordentlig.

blocks.translation: Gladly. Only then do I function properly.

spans.value: Nora and Elias repeatedly begin with the information that matters most: tomorrow, before nine, first, only under one condition, never, or when Elias arrives. Moving information to the beginning in this way is called
fronting
. Norwegian permits many kinds of information in this opening position, but the move affects the order of the main clause.
You already know the ordinary main-clause order:

no.value: Vi åpner reparasjonskafeen i morgen.

en.value: We are opening the repair café tomorrow.

spans.value: The subject vi comes first, followed by the verb åpner. Nora can instead make the time the starting point:

no.value: I morgen åpner vi reparasjonskafeen.

en.value: Tomorrow we are opening the repair café.

spans.value: Once i morgen occupies the first position, the subject cannot remain directly before the verb. The verb must come next:

no.value: I morgen åpner vi reparasjonskafeen.

en.value: Tomorrow we are opening the repair café.

no.value: I morgen vi åpner reparasjonskafeen.

en.value: Tomorrow we are opening the repair café.

spans.value: This is the
verb-second rule
, often called the
V2 rule
. In a Norwegian main clause, the
finite verb (finit verb)
occupies the second position. The finite verb is the verb marked for tense or, in a verb group, the modal or auxiliary that carries the tense.
The compact pattern is:
Fronted element + finite verb + subject + rest of the clause
Compare the neutral and fronted versions:

no.value: Nora setter fram bordene først.

en.value: Nora puts out the tables first.

no.value: Først setter Nora fram bordene.

en.value: First Nora puts out the tables.

no.value: Elias kan lage kaffe på kjøkkenet.

en.value: Elias can make coffee in the kitchen.

no.value: På kjøkkenet kan Elias lage kaffe.

en.value: In the kitchen Elias can make coffee.

no.value: De har arrangert reparasjonskafeen her før.

en.value: They have organized the repair café here before.

no.value: Her har de arrangert reparasjonskafeen før.

en.value: They have organized the repair café here before.

spans.value: In the last two fronted sentences, only the finite verb moves ahead of the subject:

items.value: In kan lage, kan is finite.
In har arrangert, har is finite.

spans.value: The other verb remains later in the clause.
A position can contain more than one word. På kjøkkenet is one fronted element, and i morgen tidlig is also one element. Count meaningful clause parts, not individual words:

no.value: I morgen tidlig kommer elektrikeren.

en.value: Tomorrow morning the electrician is coming.

spans.value: Here i morgen tidlig fills the first position. Kommer is second, and elektrikeren follows it.
Fronting does not normally change the basic event. It changes what the speaker presents first.

no.value: Vi åpner dørene klokka ni.

en.value: We open the doors at nine.

no.value: Klokka ni åpner vi dørene.

en.value: At nine we open the doors.

spans.value: Both sentences describe the same opening time. The second version uses klokka ni as the starting point, perhaps because the time is especially relevant.
A place can be fronted:

no.value: Nora oppbevarer verktøyet på kjøkkenet.

en.value: Nora keeps the tools in the kitchen.

no.value: På kjøkkenet oppbevarer Nora verktøyet.

en.value: In the kitchen Nora keeps the tools.

spans.value: A sequence word can be fronted:

no.value: Vi lager kaffe først.

en.value: We make coffee first.

no.value: Først lager vi kaffe.

en.value: First we make coffee.

spans.value: A longer time expression can be fronted:

no.value: Elias rydder lokalet etter det siste besøket.

en.value: Elias tidies the room after the last visitor.

no.value: Etter det siste besøket rydder Elias lokalet.

en.value: After the last visitor, Elias tidies the room.

spans.value: A common misconception is that fronting requires an extra verb or creates a question. It does neither. The subject follows the finite verb, as it does in many questions, but a fronted statement remains a statement:

no.value: I dag kommer Elias med bussen.

en.value: Today Elias is coming by bus.

no.value: Kommer Elias med bussen i dag?

en.value: Is Elias coming by bus today?

spans.value: The first sentence begins with a time expression and gives information. The second begins with the verb and asks a question.

sections.title: When there is more than one verb

spans.value: V2 concerns the finite verb, not every verb in the sentence.

no.value: Vi skal åpne dørene snart.

en.value: We are going to open the doors soon.

no.value: Snart skal vi åpne dørene.

en.value: Soon we are going to open the doors.

spans.value: The finite verb is skal. The infinitive åpne remains after the subject.

no.value: Nora har kjøpt ny kaffe.

en.value: Nora has bought new coffee.

no.value: Til i morgen har Nora kjøpt ny kaffe.

en.value: For tomorrow Nora has bought new coffee.

spans.value: The finite verb is har. The participle kjøpt remains later.

no.value: Elias må ta en tidligere buss på lørdag.

en.value: Elias must take an earlier bus on Saturday.

no.value: På lørdag må Elias ta en tidligere buss.

en.value: On Saturday Elias must take an earlier bus.

spans.value: Only må takes the V2 position.
A frequent error is to move the main content verb instead of the finite auxiliary:

no.value: På lørdag ta Elias må en tidligere buss.

en.value: On Saturday Elias must take an earlier bus.

spans.value: The correct order is:

no.value: På lørdag må Elias ta en tidligere buss.

en.value: On Saturday Elias must take an earlier bus.

spans.value: The V2 rule is especially important when a sentence begins with a negative or restrictive expression. These openings emphasize that something never happens, rarely happens, happens only in one situation, or does not happen before a certain point.
In the dialogue, Elias says:

no.value: Aldri har den vært så forsinket som i går.

en.value: It has never been as late as it was yesterday.

spans.value: Aldri fills the first position. Har is the finite verb, so it comes immediately afterward. The subject den follows har.
Compare:

no.value: Bussen har aldri vært så forsinket før.

en.value: The bus has never been this late before.

no.value: Aldri har bussen vært så forsinket før.

en.value: Never before has the bus been this late.

spans.value: The first sentence is neutral. The second gives aldri strong emphasis.
Other negative or restrictive openings follow the same pattern:

no.value: Sjelden kommer Elias for sent.

en.value: Elias rarely arrives late.

no.value: Ikke før klokka ni åpner Nora dørene.

en.value: Nora does not open the doors until nine.

no.value: Bare da forstår Elias problemet.

en.value: Only then does Elias understand the problem.

no.value: Først etter møtet kan de rydde lokalet.

en.value: Only after the meeting can they tidy the room.

no.value: Bare på lørdager bruker de det store rommet.

en.value: They use the large room only on Saturdays.

spans.value: English may use do, does, or did in translations such as Only then does Elias understand. Norwegian does not add an equivalent of English do. It places the existing finite verb in second position:

no.value: Bare da forstår Elias problemet.

en.value: Only then does Elias understand the problem.

no.value: Bare da gjør Elias forstå problemet.

en.value: Only then does Elias understand the problem.

spans.value: The main-clause rule remains simple even when the opening sounds emphatic:
Negative or restrictive opening + finite verb + subject + rest
Another likely error is retaining subject-first order:

no.value: Aldri bussen er i rute.

en.value: The bus is never on time.

spans.value: With aldri fronted, the finite verb must be second:

no.value: Aldri er bussen i rute.

en.value: The bus is never on time.

spans.value: That sentence is grammatically possible but strongly emphatic. In ordinary neutral speech, the following version will often sound more natural:

no.value: Bussen er aldri i rute.

en.value: The bus is never on time.

spans.value: Fronting is therefore both a word-order choice and an information choice. Use it when the opening deserves attention.
Main-clause inversion must not be carried into a subordinate clause. A
subordinate clause (leddsetning)
begins with a word such as at, fordi, hvis, or når and forms part of a larger sentence.
Nora says:

no.value: Jeg vet at bussen ikke alltid er i rute.

en.value: I know that the bus isn’t always on time.

spans.value: Inside the subordinate clause, the order is:
at + subject + ikke + finite verb

no.value: at bussen ikke alltid er i rute

en.value: that the bus isn’t always on time

spans.value: Do not apply main-clause inversion inside it:

no.value: Jeg vet at er bussen ikke alltid i rute.

en.value: I know that the bus isn’t always on time.

spans.value: Compare a fronted main clause with a subordinate clause:

no.value: I dag kan Elias ikke komme tidlig.

en.value: Today Elias cannot come early.

no.value: Nora vet at Elias ikke kan komme tidlig.

en.value: Nora knows that Elias cannot come early.

spans.value: In the first sentence, i dag is fronted in a main clause, so kan precedes Elias. In the second, at introduces a subordinate clause, so Elias remains before kan. The negative ikke also comes before the finite verb in that subordinate clause.
The same boundary appears with fordi:

no.value: I dag tar Elias bussen.

en.value: Today Elias takes the bus.

no.value: Elias tar bussen fordi han ikke kan kjøre.

en.value: Elias takes the bus because he cannot drive.

no.value: Elias tar bussen fordi kan han ikke kjøre.

en.value: Elias takes the bus because he cannot drive.

spans.value: The main-clause pattern i dag kan Elias does not license fordi kan han.

sections.title: When a whole subordinate clause comes first

spans.value: A complete subordinate clause can itself be the fronted element of a main clause. This creates two word-order decisions:

items.value: Keep ordinary subordinate-clause order inside the opening clause.
Put the finite verb of the following main clause in second position.

spans.value: Nora says:

no.value: Når du kommer, kan du lage kaffe.

en.value: When you arrive, you can make coffee.

spans.value: The entire unit når du kommer occupies the first position of the full sentence. The main-clause finite verb kan follows it, and then comes the main-clause subject du.
Inside the subordinate clause, the order remains når + du + kommer. There is no inversion there.
Compare:

no.value: Du kan lage kaffe når du kommer.

en.value: You can make coffee when you arrive.

no.value: Når du kommer, kan du lage kaffe.

en.value: When you arrive, you can make coffee.

spans.value: The subordinate clause has moved, but its internal order has not changed. The following main clause now uses V2 inversion.
The same pattern works with hvis:

no.value: Elias kommer til tiden hvis bussen er i rute.

en.value: Elias arrives on time if the bus is on schedule.

no.value: Hvis bussen er i rute, kommer Elias til tiden.

en.value: If the bus is on schedule, Elias arrives on time.

spans.value: A restrictive word can be added before the subordinate clause:

no.value: Bare hvis bussen er i rute, kommer Elias til tiden.

en.value: Only if the bus is on schedule does Elias arrive on time.

spans.value: Notice both boundaries:

items.value: Inside the subordinate clause: bussen er
In the following main clause: kommer Elias

spans.value: An incorrect version may invert both clauses:

no.value: Bare hvis er bussen i rute, kommer Elias til tiden.

en.value: Only if the bus is on schedule does Elias arrive on time.

spans.value: The main-clause inversion is correct, but the subordinate clause has been incorrectly inverted. The correct sentence is:

no.value: Bare hvis bussen er i rute, kommer Elias til tiden.

en.value: Only if the bus is on schedule does Elias arrive on time.

spans.value: A fronted subordinate clause may contain a negative:

no.value: Hvis bussen ikke kommer, tar Elias en taxi.

en.value: If the bus does not come, Elias takes a taxi.

spans.value: Inside the opening clause, bussen precedes ikke and kommer. After the entire opening clause, tar is the finite main-clause verb and Elias is the main-clause subject.
At nine, Nora has prepared most of the room. Elias finally arrives.
Endelig er du her!
Bare fordi sjåføren ventet på meg, rakk jeg bussen.

blocks.translation: I caught the bus only because the driver waited for me.

spans.value: Heldigvis har jeg allerede laget kaffe.

blocks.translation: Fortunately, I have already made coffee.

spans.value: Når jeg har drukket en kopp, kan jeg sette fram verktøyet.

blocks.translation: When I have had a cup, I can put out the tools.

spans.value: Først etter at du har hjulpet meg, kan du ta pause.

blocks.translation: Only after you have helped me can you take a break.

spans.value: Aldri får jeg en rolig morgen her.

blocks.translation: I never get a quiet morning here.

spans.value: The same pattern now appears with new openings:

no.value: Endelig er du her.

en.value: Finally you’re here.

no.value: Heldigvis har jeg allerede laget kaffe.

en.value: Fortunately, I have already made coffee.

no.value: Når jeg har drukket en kopp, kan jeg sette fram verktøyet.

en.value: When I have had a cup, I can put out the tools.

spans.value: In each main clause, the finite verb follows the fronted element. Where the opening is a subordinate clause, its internal word order remains unchanged.
In a main clause:

no.value: I morgen åpner vi tidlig.

en.value: Tomorrow we open early.

no.value: Aldri kommer Elias før Nora.

en.value: Elias never arrives before Nora.

no.value: Bare da kan vi begynne.

en.value: Only then can we begin.

spans.value: Use:
Fronted element + finite verb + subject
In a subordinate clause, do not carry over that inversion:

no.value: Nora vet at Elias ikke kommer tidlig.

en.value: Nora knows that Elias is not coming early.

spans.value: When a subordinate clause is fronted, keep its internal order and invert only the following main clause:

no.value: Hvis Elias ikke kommer, åpner Nora alene.

en.value: If Elias does not come, Nora opens alone.

spans.value: Move away from the repair café. Imagine that Ingrid is meeting Jonas at a railway station, but his train is delayed. The new situation should still trigger the same grammar choices.

Without looking back, state the main-clause pattern after fronting. Then write one Norwegian sentence beginning with a negative or restrictive expression and one beginning with a subordinate clause. Check that each main-clause finite verb is second, while each subordinate clause keeps its own subject before its finite verb.

prompt.value: Rewrite «Vi åpner sideinngangen klokka åtte» with «Klokka åtte» first.

prompt.value: Rewrite «Sara skal levere nøklene på fredag» with «På fredag» first.

explanation.value: Det finitte modalverbet «skal» står på andre plass. Infinitiven «levere» står etter subjektet.

prompt.value: Put together a sentence saying that the staff can use the storage room only after closing time. Start with «Bare etter stengetid».

prompt.value: Message from Nora: «Hvor er du? Skal jeg åpne reparasjonskafeen alene?» Facts: The bus did not come. The next bus leaves at 9:20. You will arrive at ten if the bus is on time. Reply to Nora in Norwegian. Include all the facts, ask «Kan du åpne uten meg?», and start at least one main clause with a time or condition phrase.

explanation.value: Et godt svar til Nora bruker de oppgitte faktaene. Når et tids- eller vilkårsuttrykk står først i hovedsetningen, kommer det finitte verbet foran subjektet. Leddsetninger beholder subjektet foran det finitte verbet.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against reply-purpose, supplied-facts, conditional-arrival, norwegian-response, and v2-and-boundary-observation. Treat every listed criterion as required and accept natural Norwegian wording for the condition.

criteria.instruction: The response is a reply to Nora that explains the delay and gives the plan.
The response conveys the delay and the plan: that «Bussen kom ikke», when the next bus leaves, when the learner arrives, and asks «Kan du åpne uten meg?»
States that the speaker arrives at ten if the bus is on schedule, using a natural subordinate condition such as hvis bussen er i rute. Do not require the stronger meaning only if.
The response starts at least one main clause with a time or condition expression, placing its finite verb before its subject.
